questions.q: A spring has a spring constant of 25 N/m. Calculate the force needed to extend it by 0.20 m (within the limit of proportionality).
questions.explain: F = ke = 25 × 0.20 = 5 N. Force is proportional to extension for an elastic spring within its limit of proportionality.

questions.q: A spanner is used to turn a nut. A force of 40 N is applied at a perpendicular distance of 0.15 m from the pivot. Calculate the moment.
questions.explain: M = Fd = 40 × 0.15 = 6 N m, where d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

questions.q: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.50 m². Calculate the pressure.
questions.explain: p = F/A = 200 ÷ 0.50 = 400 Pa. Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals (N/m²).

questions.q: What does it mean if a spring is stretched beyond its limit of proportionality?
options: The extension is no longer directly proportional to the force
No more force is needed to stretch it
questions.explain: Beyond the limit of proportionality the force–extension graph is no longer a straight line, so extension is no longer directly proportional to force (and deformation may become inelastic).

questions.q: A spring extends by 0.12 m when a force of 9.0 N is applied. Calculate the spring constant.
questions.explain: Rearranging F = ke gives k = F/e = 9.0 / 0.12 = 75 N/m.

questions.q: A spring of spring constant 200 N/m is extended by 0.10 m (within its limit of proportionality). Calculate the elastic potential energy stored.
A spring with spring constant 50 N/m is stretched by 0.40 m. Calculate the elastic potential energy stored (within the limit of proportionality).
questions.explain: EPE = ½ke² = ½ × 50 × 0.40² = ½ × 50 × 0.16 = 4 J. Note the extension is squared, so doubling the extension quadruples the stored energy.

questions.q: What is the difference between elastic and inelastic deformation?
options: Elastic deformation is permanent; inelastic returns to shape
Elastic deformation returns to the original shape when the force is removed; inelastic does not
questions.explain: In elastic deformation the object returns to its original shape once the force is removed. In inelastic (plastic) deformation it does not fully return — it is permanently changed.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph for a spring obeying Hooke's law, the line is:
options: A straight line through the origin
questions.explain: While a spring obeys Hooke's law, force is directly proportional to extension, so the force–extension graph is a straight line through the origin. The gradient equals the spring constant k.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph, what does the gradient of the straight (linear) region represent?
questions.explain: For the linear region, F = ke, so the gradient (force ÷ extension) is the spring constant k. The area under the line gives the elastic potential energy stored.

questions.q: A force of 600 N is spread over an area of 1.5 m². Calculate the pressure.
Calculate the pressure due to a column of water 5.0 m deep. (density of water ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 N/kg)
questions.explain: p = hρg = 5.0 × 1000 × 9.8 = 49 000 Pa. Pressure in a fluid increases with depth.

questions.q: A diver is 20 m below the surface of seawater of density 1030 kg/m³ (g = 9.8 N/kg). Calculate the pressure due to the water alone.
questions.explain: p = hρg = 20 × 1030 × 9.8 = 201 880 Pa. (The total pressure on the diver would also include atmospheric pressure pushing down on the surface.)

questions.q: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as you go higher up a mountain?
options: There is less air (a shorter column of air) above you pressing down
questions.explain: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air above. Higher up, there is less air above you and it is less dense, so the pressure is lower.

questions.q: An object is partly submerged in water. What causes the upthrust on it?
options: The water pressure is greater on the bottom than on the top of the object
The object is lighter than air
questions.explain: Pressure in a fluid increases with depth, so the upward pressure on the bottom of the object is greater than the downward pressure on its top. This difference produces a net upward force called upthrust.

questions.q: An object floats on water. How does the upthrust compare with the object's weight?
options: Upthrust is greater than the weight
Upthrust is less than the weight
questions.explain: A floating object is in equilibrium, so the upthrust (upward) exactly balances the weight (downward). If upthrust were less, it would sink; if more, it would rise.

questions.q: A force of 50 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.30 m from a pivot. Calculate the moment.
A see-saw is balanced. A child of weight 300 N sits 1.0 m from the pivot. Where must a 150 N child sit on the other side to balance it?
questions.explain: For balance, the moments are equal: 300 × 1.0 = 150 × d, so d = 300/150 = 2.0 m. The lighter child must sit further from the pivot.
